title: Cech computation for componentwise acyclic sheaves on a total slice site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $X\in\mathcal C$, and let $U_\bullet$ be any simplicial object of $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] with an augmentation $U_\bullet\to X$ (a natural map to the constant simplicial object $X$). Give the slice sites their induced topologies. The total topos $\mathcal T=\mathrm{Sh}((\mathcal C/U_\bullet)_{total})$ has sheaves given by families $F_p$ on $\mathcal C/U_p$ and transition maps $u_\alpha^{-1}F_p\to F_q$ for structure maps $u_\alpha:U_q\to U_p$, satisfying identity and composition. Write $b:\mathcal T\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C/X)$ for the augmentation and $b_p:\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C/U_p)\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C/X)$ for localization [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. For an abelian sheaf $G$ on $\mathcal C/U_p$ and $T\to X$, localization direct image is $(b_{p,*}G)(T)=G(T\times_XU_p\to U_p)$. For an abelian sheaf $F$ on $\mathcal T$, form the nonnegative cochain complex $C_b(F)^p=b_{p,*}F_p$ with the alternating sum of the face maps as differential; each face map is induced by $F_p\to u_{i,*}u_i^{-1}F_p\to u_{i,*}F_{p+1}$ and $b_{p+1}=b_pu_i$. Let $e:b_*F\to b_{0,*}F_0=C_b(F)^0$ be the map adjoint, under $b_0^{-1}\dashv b_{0,*}$, to the degree-zero component $(b^{-1}b_*F)_0=b_0^{-1}b_*F\to F_0$ of the counit $b^{-1}b_*F\to F$. Then $e$ identifies
$$b_*F=\ker\bigl(C_b(F)^0\longrightarrow C_b(F)^1\bigr).$$ If $R^q b_{p,*}F_p=0$ for every $p\geq0$ and $q>0$ (right derived functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive]), there is a natural isomorphism
$$C_b(F)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rb_*F\quad\text{in }D^+(\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C/X))$$
[def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its map on $H^0$ is the identity of $b_*F$ under the displayed kernel identification and $H^0(Rb_*F)=b_*F$. Here $F$ on the right is placed in degree zero. No hypercover or cartesian-transition hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0D79, lemma-augmentation-cech-complex, and Tag 0D7A, lemma-augmentation-spectral-sequence, including its double-complex proof; representable slice-site case in section-hypercovering. The canonical comparison is the double-complex comparison in that proof.

external.place: Tag 09W9, lemma-relocalize-given-fibre-products (3), the displayed direct-image evaluation formula.

proof.text: A morphism from an abelian sheaf $G$ on $\mathcal C/X$ to $b_*F$ is, by the augmentation adjunction, a compatible family of maps $b_p^{-1}G\to F_p$. Its degree-zero component is a map $b_0^{-1}G\to F_0$. Compatibility with the two maps $[0]\rightrightarrows[1]$ is exactly that this component factors through the kernel of $C_b(F)^0\to C_b(F)^1$. Conversely, from such a kernel map, continue along any vertex $[0]\to[p]$; any two vertices of $[p]$ are the endpoints of an order-preserving map $[1]\to[p]$, so the kernel equality makes the continuations agree. They then satisfy all simplicial identities and give a unique compatible family. Under the adjunction, the resulting map is precisely the map $e$ defined as the mate of the degree-zero counit component. Therefore $e$ identifies $b_*F$ with the displayed kernel.

source.place: Tag 0D79, lemma-augmentation-cech-complex, vertex/edge equalizer argument and the definition of the degree-zero adjoint map.

proof.text:
Apply the augmentation spectral sequence for a total simplicial site to $F$. It gives a natural comparison $\kappa_F:C_b(F)\to Rb_*F$ and a first-quadrant spectral sequence
$$E_1^{p,q}=R^q b_{p,*}F_p\Longrightarrow H^{p+q}(Rb_*F),$$
with first differential the alternating sum of the face maps. The term in row $q=0$ is exactly $C_b(F)^p=b_{p,*}F_p$, with its stated differential.

source.place: Tag 0D7A, lemma-augmentation-spectral-sequence, double-complex construction and E_1 differential.

proof.text: By the hypothesis $R^q b_{p,*}F_p=0$ for every $q>0$, every positive row of this first-quadrant spectral sequence is zero. Hence the sequence collapses at its first page, and the cohomology of $\kappa_F$ is an isomorphism in every degree: the abutment in degree $n$ is the cohomology of the row $q=0$, namely $H^n(C_b(F))$. The bounded-below derived-category criterion [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology] then makes $\kappa_F$ an isomorphism in $D^+(\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C/X))$. In degree zero, the helper states that $H^0(\kappa_F)\circ e$ is the canonical identification $b_*F=H^0(Rb_*F)$; since Step 1 shows that $e$ maps $b_*F$ isomorphically onto $\ker(C_b(F)^0\to C_b(F)^1)=H^0(C_b(F))$, $H^0(\kappa_F)$ is the identity of $b_*F$ under these identifications, which is the stated normalization.

split_report.summary: Split the arbitrary-site Cech computation into the vertex/edge kernel identification and a new statement-only augmentation spectral sequence. No hypotheses were added.
